previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with HLA-B27-positive ankylosing spondylitis and a history of chronic pain and recurrent nausea, was admitted with nausea, vomiting, and fever attributed to an upper respiratory infection. He reported that febrile illnesses often trigger vomiting, which was unresponsive to ondansetron but improved with promethazine and lorazepam. Initial evaluation revealed no bacterial infection on chest X-ray, urine, or blood work, and he received IV fluids for mild dehydration. Though back pain was not a primary complaint, he experienced a flare in thoracic pain during admission. A detailed discussion about pain management ensued, during which he expressed interest in transitioning from short-acting hydrocodone to a long-acting opioid formulation to stabilize his pain and improve function, though no change was made during the hospitalization. He acknowledged the risks and emphasized his motivation to lose weight and improve his health once pain was better controlled. He engaged in discussions about multidisciplinary strategies, including pain psychology and weight management. He stabilized clinically, remained afebrile, and had no further vomiting. He was discharged home on his prior medications with follow-up planned in primary care and pain psychology.

___ pain at rest, that increases to a ___ with regards to 
severity with any movement. He states that the pain is localized 
mainly to the bony prominences of his spine with accompanied 
paraspinal pain, and that this pain wraps around to his anterior 
chest wall, where he feels pain at the joints along his sternum, 
specifically at the sternocostal articulations. Patient reports 
that any ambulation exacerbates the pain, to the point that

to feel short of breath over short distances (ambulating to the 
bathroom, as well as ambulating in the grocery store). 
Additionally, patient has noted that he has had worsening L hip

feels like worsening of his chronic hip joint pain.

changes in bowel movements, and further denies any paresthesias

note that he has gained 30lbs over the past year, and 
intermittently experiences night sweats. He further had a ""GI 
bug"" with nausea and vomiting and subjective fevers that self 
resolved 1 month prior but has otherwise been at his baseline 
health. 

With regards to recent medication changes, patient notes that he 
is on chronic po dilaudid at home, and has recently been 
undertaking a slow taper of his dosage from Dilaudid 8mg q4h to 
q6h over the last 30 days with the help of his PCP. Furthermore, 
at the onset of his symptoms, he had just completed a taper off 
sertraline while uptitrating Cymbalta, of which he takes 30mg 
BID. Furthermore, patient notes that he has recently completed a 
7 day course of Keflex for a skin infection on his abdomen.

In the ED, patient was assessed with vital signs which were 
within normal limits T98.1 HR 82 BP 162/93 (143-164/76-124) RR18

WBC: 8.5 Hgb: 12.5 Plt: 336. Imaging was notable for a CXR which 
showed no acute process and plain film of the hip which was 
negative for any new fracture or dislocations,and only notable 
for osteoarthritic changes of the hip joints bilaterally. Due to 
low risk factors for PE and physical exam pointing to 
MSK/inflammatory etiology, cardiac/PE/DVT workup was 
deferred.Patient was given IV dilaudid 1mg x5, a total of 18mg 
po dilaudid (4mg x2, 8mg x1, 10mg x1), toradol IV 30mg x1, as 
well as home Cymbalta 30mg over a 12h period. However, despite 
this aggressive pain control regimen in the ED, patient had 
difficult to control pain. Simple movement of his torso or his 
left arm or left hip continued to cause him severe pain, and 
thus he was admitted for pain control and further workup.

Of note, patients history of AS officially dates back to the 
year ___, at which time he was diagnosed with sacroiliitis 
based on abnormal MRI and inflammatory low back pain (pt further 
reports that he has had low back pain since age ___ consistent 
with bilateral sacroiliitis). He is seen by Rheumatology and in 
Pain clinic, and has trialed  multiple immunosuppressive 
medications including sulfasalazine, etanercept, adalimumab, 
infliximab and most recently one dose of golimumab in ___, which he self-discontinued due to infectious complications 
including a facial infection treated with antibiotics followed

require antibiotics, and a fungal infection in the skin folds of 
the
groin. He was formally evaluated by infectious disease during a 
prior admission at which time it was determined there was no 
gross contraindication to TNF inhibitor therapy in treatment of 
his disease. Out of all these medications, he had the most 
positive result with infliximab. However, due to various 
complications on the above medications, patient is currently 
declining initiating biologic/immunosuppressive therapy at this 
time, which has been documented multiple times by his rheum/pain 
clinic providers. He has now been off of all treatment for 
ankylosing spondylitis since ___.

He is currently taking 8 mg of p.o. Dilaudid, which he has

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ PMHx of HLA-B27-positive ankylosing 
spondylitis, not on immunosuppressive agents (with prior failure 
of sulfasalazine, etanercept, adalimumab, infliximab, golimumab) 
with multiple hospitalizations for back pain and abdominal 
pain/n/v with recent discharge on ___ for recurrent back 
pain, now presenting with worsening upper back pain and anterior 
chest wall/sterncostal articulation pain for the past 6 days and 
2 days of significant hip pain likely due to worsening of known 
ankylosing spondylitis in the setting of not being on 
immunosuppressive therapy and recent narcotic tapering and 
adjustment of adjunctive pain medication regimen.

# Back pain
# Anterior chest wall / sternocostal articulation pain
# Ankylosing spondylitis.
Patients presentation and exam was notable for joint pain 
tenderness over the T1-T4 and T10 transverse processes, 
tenderness diffusely over the anterior chest specifically at the 
sternocostal articulations, and L hip pain. Patient had no focal 
neurologic deficits, with no issues with urinary/stool 
continence, full strength and no parasthesias in the upper or 
lower extremities making cord compression an unlikely etiology, 
and lab workup was reassuring making infectious etiology/abscess 
unlikely. With regards to pts chest pain, his pain was worsened 
with palpation at the sternocostal articulations indicating a 
MSK etiology rather than cardiogenic in nature. Reassuringly, 
patients EKG was unremarkable with no evidence of acute ischemic 
changes. Patients current presentation is likely due to 
worsening of his known Ankylosing spondylitis pain while not on 
an immunosuppressive agents, and may have been further 
worsesned./exacerbated in the setting of downtitration of his po 
dilaudid and weaning from sertraline to cymbalta. Patient has 
had frequent hospitalizations for back pain, with patient 
evaluated by the chronic pain service during his ___ and 
___ admissions. Unfortunately pt  remains uninterested in 
trying any biologic treatments given concern for infection, 
making control of his inflammatory arthropathy difficult in this 
setting, as patient has declined all immunosuppressive therapy 
and has continued only opioid based pain control. On this 
admission, pts ESR was elevated to 74, which is the highest it 
has been previously (previously ranging from 40-50, as high as 
68 in ___ and CRP also elevated to 18.1 (highest it has been 
since ___, where it was 35.7). Elevation of inflammatory 
markers may be consistent with worsening of his underlying 
ankylosing spondylitis. Pt was stabilized on a regimen of 
Dilaudid 8mg q4h, Tylenol 1gm q8h and topical lidocaine cream. 
Patients Cymbalta was further increased to 30mg BID. Patient was 
further evaluated by Chronic Pain service who carried out 
trigger point injections which provided considerable reduction 
of patients pain. Plan was made for patient to continue on 
Dilaudid 8mg q4h, and to be seen in Chronic pain clinic to 
establish a mutli-modal approach to his pain by assessing his 
pain medication requirement, repeat of trigger point injections 
on an as needed basis, working with pain psychiatrist for CBT 
and biofeedback as well as social work to work on his anxiety 
and pain requirements. Patient was agreeable to this approach, 
and plan was made for patient to be discharged with followup 
appointments with his PCP and to be seen in pain clinic. 
Furthermore, patient was advised to work with his outpatient 
Rheumatologist to consider alternative immunosuppressive 
regimens, although currently he is currently resistant to 
initiating any new disease modifying therapies at this time.

# BLE edema: on this admission, pt was continued on home Lasix 
20 mg daily

# HTN: on this admission, patient was continued on home 
lisinopril 20mg daily

# Asthma: on this admission, patient was continued on home
